vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: lastfm-spotify-playlists
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle is a legitimate integration for creating Spotify playlists using Last.fm's recommendation engine. It handles API credentials through environment variables or local configuration files in the user's home directory (~/.openclaw/) and implements a standard OAuth flow for Spotify authentication using a temporary local HTTP server. The code in scripts like lastfm_spotify_playlist_pipeline.py and spotify_common.py is well-structured, follows its stated purpose, and contains no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions match its description: it uses Last.fm for discovery and Spotify for search/playlist creation and requires just your Last.fm and Spotify credentials — no hidden endpoints or obvious malicious behavior.

dimensions.detail: The name/description, SKILL.md, and the included scripts consistently implement Last.fm-based discovery + Spotify playlist creation. One minor inconsistency: the registry metadata lists no required environment variables, but the code expects Last.fm and Spotify credentials (via env vars or local credential files). Functionality requested (API keys, OAuth) is appropriate for the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts limit actions to fetching Last.fm data, searching Spotify, performing OAuth, creating playlists, and writing a local token file. Instructions do not instruct reading or exfiltrating unrelated system files or sending data to unexpected endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only plus bundled scripts). Scripts run locally and use standard libraries and direct HTTPS calls to Last.fm and Spotify; no downloads from untrusted URLs or archive extraction was observed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill legitimately needs Last.fm API key/username and Spotify client_id/client_secret/redirect_uri plus a token file. The package references environment variables (LASTFM_*, SPOTIFY_*) and local files under ~/.openclaw, which are proportionate, but the registry metadata did not declare these required env vars—users should be aware credentials are necessary and stored locally.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent platform privileges or always-enabled status. It stores OAuth tokens and credentials under ~/.openclaw (a reasonable, isolated location) and runs a short-lived local HTTP server during OAuth — expected for a local OAuth flow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it claims. Before installing or running it: (1) be prepared to provide Last.fm API key/username and Spotify client_id/client_secret/redirect_uri (via environment variables or the ~/.openclaw JSON files); the registry metadata did not list these, so supply them manually. (2) The Spotify auth flow will open a browser and run a temporary local HTTP server (default 127.0.0.1:8888) to capture the OAuth code — ensure this redirect URI is safe and expected. (3) Tokens are saved to ~/.openclaw/spotify-token.json; review and protect that file. (4) Review the included scripts yourself if you have doubts — they perform network calls to Last.fm and api.spotify.com only. (5) Do not put real secrets into the package; follow references/credentials.md for local storage. If you want extra assurance, run the scripts in a restricted environment or examine the code before running.
